sentences.text: In the cold Arctic, many animals live.
They have special ways to survive.
Let's learn about some of them.
First, there is the polar bear.
Polar bears have thick fur.
This fur keeps them warm.
They also have a layer of fat.
This fat is called blubber.
Blubber helps them stay warm in icy water.
Polar bears are great swimmers.
They can swim for many miles.
They hunt seals for food.
Next, we have the Arctic fox.
The Arctic fox has white fur in winter.
This fur helps it hide in the snow.
In summer, its fur turns brown.
This helps it hide on the rocks and plants.
The Arctic fox has small ears.
Small ears help keep it warm.
It eats small animals and birds.
Another animal is the caribou.
Caribou are also called reindeer.
They have thick fur, too.
Their fur traps air.
This air keeps them warm.
Caribou have big hooves.
These hooves help them walk on snow.
They eat plants and moss.
The snowy owl is another Arctic animal.
It has white feathers.
These feathers help it hide in the snow.
The snowy owl has sharp claws.
It uses these claws to catch food.
It eats small animals like mice.
Lastly, we have the walrus.
Walruses have thick skin.
They also have blubber.
Blubber keeps them warm.
Walruses have long tusks.
They use these tusks to break ice.
They also use them to climb out of the water.
Walruses eat clams and other sea animals.
These animals are amazing.
They have special ways to live in the Arctic.
Their adaptations help them survive the cold.
